subject: Follow-up: data handling clarifications & telemetry vendor review — next steps
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sara Gomez <sara@finhealth.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Meeting follow-up: data handling & telemetry questions

Hi Sara — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can scope the security review and procurement path:

Summary of what we heard on the call:
- You plan to use Redwood to power natural language features in your customer support product; traffic will include both end-customer text and metadata from support sessions.
- Analytics/telemetry will be routed to your analytics stack (Segment) and to Datadog for app logs.
- Procurement will likely flow through AWS Marketplace for initial proof-of-concept.

Clarifying questions (can you confirm these items by EOD Monday?):
1) Data classification: which fields in the support payload are considered PII/sensitive (e.g., full name, account number, SSN-like identifiers)? A simple list or data map is fine.
2) Retention: desired retention window for raw transcripts and derived embeddings? You mentioned short-term and long-term buckets during the call — please confirm months for each.
3) Logging & audit: what level of request/response logging do you need retained (request IDs, full request bodies, token sampling)? Do you require immutable audit logs for a specific duration?
4) Data residency: Do you require EU-only residency for EU customers, or is regional routing sufficient?
5) Subprocessors/third parties: confirm vendors that will receive telemetry or logs (Segment, Datadog, AWS Marketplace flow, any others).

Attached: discovery-data-requests.pdf (short checklist) — fills in the items above if helpful.

If it's useful we can set a 30-min security deep-dive with our security engineer (Priyom) and Diego from platform to walk through telemetry flows. Suggested time slots: Tue/Wed morning PT.

Thanks — Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Redwood Inference

From: Sara Gomez <sara@finhealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: FinHealth Procurement <procurement@finhealth.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 15:45:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Meeting follow-up: data handling & telemetry questions

Hi Vanessa — thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers below (happy to expand in the deep-dive):

1) Data classification: primary PII in the support payload is customer full name, email, account_id (internal numeric id), and transaction reference (alphanumeric). We do NOT include PHI in support transcripts.

2) Retention: short-term transcripts = 90 days; derived embeddings = 13 months; logs for debug (truncated request metadata) = 6 months. We may request longer retention for legal holds, but those will be ad-hoc.

3) Logging & audit: we need request-level logging for SLA troubleshooting (request_id, timestamp, HTTP metadata). Full request/response bodies should be available for debug but redaction/hashing is preferred for account_id in production streams. Immutable audit logs for admin actions = 12 months.

4) Data residency: EU customer data must remain in EU region (data residency requirement). For US customers region-specific routing is fine.

5) Subprocessors: current telemetry/analytics vendors: Segment (event-level), Datadog (app logs). We also use Sentry for exception events. Marketplace flows will be via AWS Marketplace SaaS contracts.

Attaching a quick data map: FinHealth-data-map.xlsx. Procurement is cc'd here — procurement will follow up on contract questions and PO timing.

Sara Gomez
Head of Product Operations, FinHealth Inc.
sara@finhealth.com | +1 (617) 555-2233

--
Attachment: FinHealth-data-map.xlsx (stub, 1 sheet)

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 16:25:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Meeting follow-up: data handling & telemetry questions (internal)

Vanessa / Diego — quick internal note based on Sara's answers. Flagging items we should get clarified in the security deep-dive and call out what we can pre-send:

- Event-level telemetry: need a list of event names and schemas that Segment will forward to us. Confirm whether account_id is sent hashed or plain. If plain, request that it be hashed at source or that they send a salt/tokenization strategy.
- Embeddings retention: 13 months is okay; confirm if embeddings are considered derived PII by their legal team. If yes, we need to treat them as sensitive and apply stricter key management.
- Immutable audit logs (12 months) aligns with our standard audit exports, but we need to confirm S3 bucket location for EU-residency customers.
- Telemetry vendors: add Sentry to subprocessors list. We should ask for vendor contacts and an existing Data Processing Agreement (DPA) or SOC 2 reports if available.
- Marketplace: confirm whether initial onboarding uses AWS Marketplace private offers (PO via marketplace) or direct PO to Redwood (affects invoicing & procurement team involvement).

Action items I can take before the call:
- Share our standard security questionnaire link and SOC 2 redacted report. (link below)
- Prepare recommended config for hashing account identifiers and for token sampling to minimize PII exposure in logs.

Security questionnaire: https://redwood-inference.sharepoint.com/sec-questionnaires/finhealth
Redwood SOC 2 (redacted): https://redwood-inference.sharepoint.com/security/reports/soc2-redacted.pdf

Priyom
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com

--
Attachment: security-questionnaire-link.txt (link to internal SharePoint)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sara Gomez <sara@finhealth.com>, FinHealth Procurement <procurement@finhealth.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Bcc: rohan_mehta@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 18:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Meeting follow-up: data handling & telemetry questions — proposed next steps

Sara — thanks for the speedy answers and for sharing the data map. I pulled the key items into an actionable checklist so procurement and security have a clear path forward. Quoting your note on telemetry: 

> On Sun, 30 May 2027 at 15:45:12 -0700 Sara Gomez <sara@finhealth.com> wrote:
> 5) Subprocessors: current telemetry/analytics vendors: Segment (event-level), Datadog (app logs). We also use Sentry for exception events. Marketplace flows will be via AWS Marketplace SaaS contracts.

Proposed next steps / owners:
- By Mon, 2027-05-31 EOD (Sara) — confirm which event names/schemas include account_id and whether account_id will be hashed before sending to Redwood. If hashing in-source is not feasible, confirm acceptable PII tokenization approach.
- By Tue, 2027-06-01 (Procurement & Vanessa) — confirm procurement path: AWS Marketplace private offer vs. direct PO. Provide estimated PO date and any procurement constraints.
- By Wed, 2027-06-02 (Priyom & Diego) — 30-min security deep-dive to review telemetry flows, DPA/SOC 2 artifacts, and agree on retention controls for embeddings/logs. Priyom will send calendar invites.
- Priyom (internal) — share redacted SOC 2 and the pre-filled security questionnaire for FinHealth to complete prior to the deep-dive.

Additional notes:
- If FinHealth requires EU-only residency for EU customers, we will route those requests to our EU region and pin model serving to EU-hosted instances. We'll include a note about audit log S3 location in the deep-dive.
- Attachment checklist: discovery-data-requests.pdf, FinHealth-data-map.xlsx, security questionnaire link.

Would you like me to loop in our legal contact (Rohan Mehta) now or after procurement confirms PO path? I bcc'd Rohan for visibility.

Thanks — I will send a calendar invite for the Wed slot once Sara confirms event schema details.

Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
